title.en: Ramayana — Aranyakanda (Wikipedia summary story — Telugu, full text)

lessons.title: Lesson 01 — The Slaying of Viradha
lessons.content:
After receiving blessings from Sage Atri and Anasuya, Sita, Rama, and Lakshmana proceeded into the Dandaka forest. In a hermitage, the sages greeted them with auspicious blessings and entreated Rama to protect them. After resting there for the night, they continued their journey and entered a terrifying dense forest.

There, a demon named Viradha, with a huge misshapen body, confronted them. He had impaled three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten deer, and a large elephant head on his spear for leisurely eating. He was originally the Gandharva Tumburu but became a demon due to Kubera's curse and was blessed to be invulnerable to weapons. Only Rama could free him from the curse. Viradha tried to abduct Sita but, angered by Rama’s sharp arrows, released her and seized Rama and Lakshmana instead.

Rama and Lakshmana severed Viradha’s arms. Freed from the curse, Viradha realized who they were and advised them to go to Sage Sharabhanga’s hermitage. Digging a pit large enough for an elephant, Rama and Lakshmana buried his body.

lessons.title: Lesson 02 — Visiting the Hermitages
lessons.content:
Sage Sharabhanga, who had attained Brahma-realization, was waiting only for Rama before departing to Brahmaloka. He offered his earned merit to Rama and advised them to visit Sage Sutikshna next. Afterwards, Sharabhanga entered the fire through yogic powers and reached Brahmaloka.

Many sages approached Rama, describing the troubles caused by demons. Rama promised to protect them, giving them assurance. Sita, Rama, and Lakshmana then visited Sutikshna’s hermitage. This sage, too, was waiting for Rama before departing to the divine realms and welcomed them with fruits and roots. After paying respects and taking leave, Rama and Lakshmana, armed with weapons and accompanied by Sita, set out to see the hermitages throughout Dandaka forest.

Sita expressed her thoughts to the weapon-bearing Rama and Lakshmana, noting that the sage’s path was very strict, disturbed by untruthful speech, illicit relations, and unnecessary violence. Carrying weapons might induce unnecessary aggression; weapons should only be used to protect the distressed. Normally, living like hermits is appropriate for the forest. She humbly acknowledged her impulsiveness and said they were already aware of their duties. Rama praised Sita’s words, confirming that he would use weapons only to protect sages who sought his refuge.

Passing through beautiful ascetic groves, Sita, Rama, and Lakshmana saw the enchanting Panchapsarasa lake. Sage Mandakarni created it with his penance and lived underwater in a secret palace, playing with apsaras, so sweet music always emanated from there. They visited many hermitages and returned to Sutikshna’s ashram, asking the way to Sage Agastya’s hermitage.

lessons.title: Lesson 03 — Visiting Agastya’s Ashram
lessons.content:
Following Sutikshna’s instructions, Sita, Rama, and Lakshmana first visited the hermitage of Agastya’s brother and accepted his hospitality. They then proceeded to Sage Agastya’s hermitage. Agastya, renowned for conquering death and stopping the Vindhya mountains from growing, destroyed the cannibals Vataapi and Ilvala, and made the southern region suitable for sages.

Sita, Rama, and Lakshmana bowed to Agastya, who welcomed them with meals befitting forest-dwellers and inquired about their welfare. He gave Rama the great Vaishnava bow crafted by Vishvakarma and praised Sita’s devotion as a wife.

lessons.title: Lesson 04 — Residence at Panchavati
lessons.content:
Agastya advised them to build a hermitage and live on the banks of the Godavari in Panchavati. On the way to Panchavati, they met Jatayu, the great vulture king, who claimed friendship with Dasharatha and promised to watch over Sita near the hermitage.

In Panchavati, Lakshmana built a beautiful leaf hut where Rama directed, making it heavenly for Sita. They lived there happily for a long time.

lessons.title: Lesson 05 — Mutilation of Surpanakha
lessons.content:
Surpanakha, the demoness and sister of Ravana, roamed freely in the forest. She was a shape-shifter. One day, she visited their hut, was enamored by Rama, and asked him to marry her. Rama and Lakshmana joked with her. Angered, she tried to devour Sita, but on Rama’s command, Lakshmana cut off Surpanakha’s nose and ears.

Surpanakha, in tears, complained to her brother Khara, who summoned fourteen powerful demons to kill Rama and Lakshmana. Rama slew them with fourteen arrows. Surpanakha further provoked Khara, insulting his competence. Enraged, he and his general Dushana attacked with a force of fourteen thousand demons, launching a fierce assault with great noise and tumult.

lessons.title: Lesson 06 — Destruction of Khara and Dushana
lessons.content:
Rama noticed ominous portents in the sky. Following Rama’s instructions, Lakshmana armed himself, took Sita, and went into a cave as a fortress. Rama donned armor, took his bow, and bravely faced the demons. Sages, gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and Charanas gathered in the sky to bless Rama and watch the battle.

Khara and his army attacked Rama with loud noises. Many demon warriors fell to Rama’s deathly arrows; the rest fled to seek refuge with Khara. Dushana angrily attacked Rama, but Rama shattered Dushana’s bow, chariot, horses, and charioteer with arrows, then broke his chest and arms. Seeing Dushana fall, the enraged Khara attacked Rama with twelve chief generals. Rama, with diamond-like arrows, killed all their captains and troops, the battlefield covered in blood and flesh.

Only Khara and Trishira remained. Trishira fiercely charged and was slain by Rama’s arrows. Khara and Rama then confronted each other, and their showers of arrows darkened the sky. Rama dismembered the giant tree Khara brought and riddled his body with arrows, causing him to bleed profusely. Khara sprang at Rama, but Rama shot a blazing arrow, knocking him to the ground.

Divine drums sounded in the sky and flowers rained down. Lakshmana, hearing the gods’ cheers, emerged from the cave with Sita and worshipped Rama, who was praised by Sita for his victory.

lessons.title: Lesson 07 — Surpanakha’s Complaint to Ravana
lessons.content:
With the death of fourteen thousand demons, Khara, Dushana, and Trishira, Surpanakha mournfully went to Lanka and heavily reproached her elder brother Ravana, warning him of impending disaster. She explained that lacking proper spies, treasury, and policies spells a king’s ruin. Their whole clan had been wiped out by Rama, the son of Dasharatha. Rama and Lakshmana were depopulating Janasthana of demons, and Sita’s beauty was matchless. Surpanakha urged Ravana to kill Rama, take Sita for himself, and redeem the demon race’s honor.

Prompted by her words, Ravana devised a plot to abduct Sita, seeking Maricha’s help to lure Rama away by transforming into a magical deer.

lessons.title: Lesson 08 — Maricha's Advice to Ravana
lessons.content:
Upon hearing Rama's name, Maricha turned pale with terror and gave Ravana well-meant counsel, saying Rama was a great hero and adherent of truth. To fight with him would bring ruin to Ravana and his race. Previously, Maricha, with the strength of a thousand elephants, had roamed the world unopposed. When he attacked Vishwamitra’s sacrifice, Rama, then just twelve years old, killed Subahu, destroyed Maricha’s demon army, and hurled Maricha into the ocean with a mighty arrow. Ever since, Maricha said, he shuddered at words starting with 'Ra', like 'Ratha' (chariot) and 'Ratna' (jewel). He advised Ravana to abandon hostility and seek refuge with Rama.

Ravana, unmoved, declared he would not change his mind even if gods pleaded. He ordered Maricha to transform into a golden deer to attract Sita and thus lure Rama and Lakshmana away from the hut. Maricha, seeing no way out, thought it better to die at Rama’s hands than Ravana’s. They set out towards Rama’s hut.

lessons.title: Lesson 09 — The Deception with the Magic Deer
lessons.content:
While Sita was collecting flowers near the hut, thinking their forest life would soon be over, she saw a beautiful golden deer sparkling with silver spots. Fascinated by its grace, she asked Rama to fetch it for her. Lakshmana strongly warned that it was a demon’s magic, and such deer don’t exist. Rama resolved to kill the demon if so and asked Lakshmana to keep Sita safe until he returned.

The deer danced and disappeared repeatedly, leading Rama far away. Realizing no use, Rama strung his bow and shot the deer, which, dying, resumed its true form as Maricha and cried out loudly for Sita and Lakshmana. Rama hurried back, fearing danger.

Hearing the cry, Sita grew fearful for Rama’s safety and pleaded with Lakshmana to help. Lakshmana insisted no one in the three worlds could defeat Rama and that the cry was a demon’s trick, but said he would stay and protect Sita as per his brother’s instructions. Sita, agitated, wrongly accused Lakshmana of wishing ill for Rama.

Lakshmana, upset by the accusation, left, fearing disaster would strike the accused mother. He prayed for the forest deities to protect Sita and, distressed by bad omens, set out to search for Rama.

lessons.title: Lesson 10 — The Abduction of Sita
lessons.content: Seeing his chance, Ravana arrived disguised as a monk and greeted Sita. As Sita awaited Rama and Lakshmana, she welcomed the fake ascetic as a guest and explained their situation and exile. Ravana then revealed his true form and asked Sita to be his wife. Sita, blazing like fire, scorned Ravana, likening him to a blade of grass and warned him of his destruction if he desired her. Ravana forcibly grabbed Sita and placed her in his chariot. Hearing her cries, Jatayu confronted Ravana fiercely.

lessons.title: Lesson 11 — The Death of Jatayu
lessons.content:
Jatayu and Ravana fought like two mountains crashing together. Ignoring Ravana’s arrows, Jatayu attacked and smashed the chariot. Enraged, Ravana cut off Jatayu’s sides, wings, and thighs. As Jatayu lay dying, Ravana departed through the sky with Sita towards Lanka. On a hill along the way, several monkeys appeared. Sita threw some jewels among them while Ravana was distracted. Ravana reached Lanka with Sita and kept her in Ashoka grove, guarded by demonesses.

Rama, meeting Lakshmana, rebuked him for leaving Sita alone. Lakshmana sorrowfully explained that Sita had driven him away with harsh words. They returned to the hut, found Sita missing, and searched desperately. Guided by some deer towards the south, they discovered the bloodied, dying Jatayu, who recounted Sita’s abduction and his own injuries before dying in Rama’s presence. Rama mourned deeply and performed Jatayu’s funeral rites. The brothers resumed their search for Sita.

lessons.title: Lesson 12 — Kabandha’s Liberation from Curse
lessons.content: Near Matanga’s hermitage, they encountered a giant demon named Kabandha with neither head nor neck, whose face was on his stomach and arms were as long as fathoms, with a mountain-like body. Kabandha was a Gandharva turned demon by a curse. He tried to eat Rama and Lakshmana but they severed his arms. Realizing they could release him from his curse, Kabandha asked them to offer his body to fire. Ascending the flames, Kabandha emerged as a Gandharva and, leaving in a swan-shaped chariot, told Rama to befriend Sugriva to help search for Sita. He advised meeting Shabari near Pampa Lake at Matanga’s hermitage, then Sugriva on Rishyamuka mountain, whose friendship would help Rama regain Sita after vanquishing all demons.

lessons.title: Lesson 13 — Shabari’s Service
lessons.content: Shabari, a devoted ascetic, was serving the sages at Matanga’s hermitage, awaiting Rama’s arrival after her gurus had already ascended to heaven. She greeted Rama and Lakshmana, offered them sweet fruits, and performed the guest ceremony. Rama inquired about her welfare, and she showed them the entire hermitage. The sages, by their penance, had brought the seven seas there. Shabari then asked to go to her gurus, and Rama, delighted, blessed her, saying she had worshipped him with great devotion and should now go happily wherever she wished. Instantly, Shabari offered her aged body to fire and ascended in a celestial chariot to join her revered gurus.

lessons.title: Lesson 14 — The Pampa Lake
lessons.content: Rama and Lakshmana explored the wonders in Matanga’s hermitage. Bathing in the seven sacred lakes, they performed rites for ancestors, feeling the troubles vanish and auspiciousness prevail. Proceeding quickly, they reached Pampa Lake, resplendent with colorful lotuses and water lilies like a jeweled carpet. Surrounded by blooming trees and pure water, the lake was breathtaking, bringing Sita to Rama’s mind. They continued towards Rishyamuka mountain to meet Sugriva, searching for Sita.
